changelog.title: Sign in, a new look, and a lot more real
notes: New: Sign in with Google (Training → top of the sidebar) — your progress follows you between PC and phone and survives reinstalling

How they arrived: walk-in, family, ambulance with a real EMS handoff (and what EMS already gave), police, nursing home, found down. Talk tab: question whoever brought them — the scene, last known well, drugs, mood, suicide talk

Real people at real rates: some swear, grab, refuse you as their nurse, vomit, wet the bed or throw the tray — often with a medical cause you can fix. Care → Behavior & safety to respond (de-escalate, security, hand off with SBAR)

Ventilator settings when intubated: rate, tidal volume, PEEP and FiO₂ all change the physiology. Big tidal volumes are flagged; weaning the FiO₂ to target is rewarded

New: Attached list under the patient bar — every line, tube and device, each removable. Extubation follows real criteria, with a spontaneous breathing trial; extubate too early and they stop breathing
IV drugs now need IV (or IO/central) access; pulling the only line stops the infusions

Fixed: the chart kept saying "respiratory rate of four, snoring airway" after intubation — the exam and nurse notes now describe the patient as they are now
Fixed: a ventilated overdose kept getting worse — the ventilator now counts as treating it
Fixed: the monitor power button jumped position when switched on/off
The top bar, vitals and patient name now stay pinned when you scroll (PC)
Monitor training: new lesson on latched alarms (why it can say SpO₂ Low at 100% — Philips factory default latching; press Silence to acknowledge)

changelog.title: Know it, or you don't pass
notes: Fixed: the right answer was usually the longest one (half of all questions, up to 98% in some topics). Every question bank was rewritten — now it is the longest only 14% of the time, so length tells you nothing

Anti-cheat: quiz questions are timed (90 s, exam 75 s), leaving the app mid-question (ChatGPT, camera, anything) forfeits it — three strikes voids the attempt; no copying question text; screenshots blocked on the phone during tests
Guess detection: answers faster than the question can be read count as guesses; three in a practice set voids the set
Cases: throwing random drugs or a pile of unrelated tests at a patient is now a critical error
Progress is saved after every answer, with a spare copy; reopening returns you to the exact page; a test left half-way picks up where it stopped. Reset now needs you to type RESET
New: your license — name, M.D., rank from Pre-clinical student to Attending, earned only by finishing everything cleanly. Clearly marked as a simulation, not a real license; an edited save voids it
New: tap any underlined word for a plain-English definition (1,334 terms)
New: Ask the teacher — type any question; answers come from the course (on the PC the local AI explains them in plain words). Off during tests and solo cases

New module: Substances — what they actually do. Vaping, smoking, cannabis, alcohol, opioids and fentanyl pills, stimulants, nitrous, inhalants and how addiction works, with the exact mechanisms. Open any time

changelog.title: Strict training, every module
notes: Training is now strict — you have to know it to get out: 9 of 10 to master a topic (one slip max, and a hint counts as a slip), 90% on module quizzes, 90% on the final exam AND 80% in every subject, 19 of 20 drills
Every quiz and the final exam are drawn fresh each attempt from the practice banks, so they can't be memorized; the final exam gives no feedback until the end

11 new training modules, each with lessons, Khan-style practice topics, a quiz, rapid-response drills and hands-on cases: Reading the labs, Procedures and surgeries, Sepsis (SSC 2026), Stroke (AHA/ASA 2026, tenecteplase), Chest pain and ACS (2025 ACC/AHA), Bradycardia and heart blocks, Anaphylaxis, Breathing failure, DKA and HHS, Electrolytes, Overdoses and antidotes

Fixes: CO2-retainer oxygen explanation corrected (V/Q mismatch and Haldane, not "hypoxic drive"); epinephrine anaphylaxis dose is 0.01 mg/kg IM up to 0.5 mg; dozens of guideline corrections across conditions

notes: Every module now teaches topic by topic like Khan Academy: lessons, then 10-question practice sets with Hint and "I don't understand this" (opens an in-depth explanation, then a fresh question). 8 of 10 without help masters a topic; the module quiz opens only when every topic is mastered

Care team: call the pharmacist (doses, allergies, interactions, reversal), respiratory therapist (airway, ABG reading), charge nurse (what you are missing) or hospitalist (they ask what YOU think)
AED mode on the crash cart, with voice prompts — analyzes, advises a shock, then 2-minute CPR cycles

changelog.title: Leads off, probes off: the equipment acts up like real life
notes: Most alarms on a real unit are the equipment, not the patient - now they are here too, using the exact IntelliVue messages from the manual
ECG: RA Lead Off, LA/LL/V/RL Lead Off, ECG Leads Off, ECG Noisy Signal - the HR shows -?-, the trace goes flat or noisy, and the light-blue INOP tone sounds
A single LA, LL or V lead off: -?- for 10 seconds, then the monitor falls back to another lead (the INOP stays until you fix it)
SpO2: Sensor Off, NoisySignal (movement or shivering), Low Perf (cold or shocked patient), Extd.Update (BP cuff on the same arm as the probe)
Turning, washing and toileting patients knocks things off; confused, restless or shivering patients pull and shake them; electrodes dry out after a day
While the ECG is off the monitor cannot alarm on the heart rate or rhythm - the SpO2 is your only warning. Leave the leads off and the monitor tech calls
Fixes in the Care tab (Equipment): stick the lead back on, change all the electrodes, put the probe back on, move it to the earlobe, move the BP cuff to the other arm, see which lead is off
Several INOPs at once take turns with an arrow, and the minimized strip shows them too

changelog.title: Alarm sounds measured from real IntelliVue monitors
notes: Every alarm sound was measured from recordings of real IntelliVue monitors (pitch, overtones, timing, how it rings) and rebuilt to match
Traditional yellow is lower (480 Hz) and Traditional red is 960 Hz with its bright overtone; both now ring out for about a second instead of cutting off
ISO red: 5 quick pulses on 481 Hz; ISO yellow: 3 pulses on 360 Hz; INOP: 2 pulses on 240 Hz
A faint room echo between pulses, at the level measured in the recordings
